editorial:
Imagine being thrown into a rough prison camp for a crime you did not even really commit. That is exactly what happens to the young girl played by Shirley Ross. She gets dragged into a mess because of her boyfriend, a crook played by Lloyd Nolan. You get to see them both struggle through six months on a prison farm where the guards are totally heartless. The vibe is pretty grim, and you will feel bad for the prisoners as they deal with mean supervisors who love to make their lives miserable. It is a classic old-school drama that focuses on how unfair the system can be.

You will probably love how the actors play their roles, especially the guards who are just plain evil. The pacing is steady, though some parts feel a bit slow by today's standards. If you enjoy seeing an innocent person fight for their dignity, you should definitely check this one out. Since it is an older flick, you might want to look for a restored version to get the best picture. Try renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection if you can find it to keep the quality high.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the prisoners can no longer stand the abuse from the guards. There is a big push for justice as the truth about the crime comes out. The innocent girl finally gets her name cleared, and the bad guards get what they deserve for being so cruel. It ends on a hopeful note where the couple finds a way to move past their mistakes and start over with a clean slate.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old crime dramas and stories about overcoming unfair odds.
